references.text: Moses wrote down all the Lord's words, which demonstrates the practice of recording God's law in writing.
God gave Moses stone tablets with the law and commandments written on them, paralleling the act of writing the law on stones.
Moses was commanded to carve out stone tablets so that God's words could be written on them.
The king was to write a copy of this law, emphasizing the importance of recording the words of the law in writing.
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, illustrating the practice of transmitting the law through written records.
Joshua made a copy of the Law of Moses on stones, fulfilling the command given in Deuteronomy 27:8.
Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal and wrote the law on the stones, just as Moses had commanded.
Habakkuk was commanded to write the vision clearly on tablets so that it could be read easily—paralleling the instruction to write the law clearly and distinctly.
